Interim Ordinary Dividend Declaration
brief: Valterra Platinum declares R57.00 per share interim dividend, comprising R32.50 base and R24.50 additional distribution.
summary: Valterra Platinum's board approved a gross interim cash dividend of R15.1 billion (R57.00 per share) on 27 July 2026. The dividend comprises a base cash dividend of R32.50 per share (40% of headline earnings, per policy) and an additional cash dividend of R24.50 per share under capital allocation framework. Payment dates are 24 August 2026 (JSE) and 8 September 2026 (LSE). For South African shareholders, standard 20% withholding tax applies unless treaty relief obtained; UK-listed shareholders receive Pound Sterling equivalent of 256.10 pence per share.
retail_take: Strong shareholder return signal reflecting robust earnings and disciplined capital allocation. Material dividend yield and additional distribution suggest confidence in operational cash generation and constrained reinvestment needs, likely reading positively for income-focused investors.

headline: Interim results and board committee change
brief: Valterra Platinum reports H1 2026 results with 4x EBITDA growth to R33.4bn, declares R57/share dividend, but three workplace fatalities mar performance.
summary: H1 2026 revenue doubled to R81.8bn driven by 85% surge in dollar PGM basket prices to US$2,801/oz and 18% higher sales volumes (1.7m oz). Adjusted EBITDA surged 406% to R33.4bn with 50% mining margin. Headline EPS jumped to R82.02 from R4.73; company declared R15.1bn total dividend (R57/share, 70% payout ratio vs 40% policy). However, three fatalities occurred during the period, prompting safety interventions. All-in sustaining costs fell 21% to US$996/3E oz. Net cash position strengthened to R23.7bn. Full-year 2026 production guidance (3.0-3.4m oz) and unit cost guidance (R19,000-R20,000/oz) reaffirmed.
retail_take: Strong financial delivery on rising commodity prices and operational improvements, with exceptional shareholder returns, likely viewed positively; however, elevated fatality count introduces ESG concern that may temper sentiment despite robust safety metrics relative to peers.

headline: Half Year Report 2026
brief: Standard Chartered publishes H1 2026 interim results; full report available from 19 August.
summary: Standard Chartered PLC submitted its 2026 Half Year Report to the Financial Conduct Authority on 29 July 2026. The document is available for inspection at the FCA's National Storage Mechanism and on the company's investor website. Physical copies will be posted to shareholders on 19 August 2026. The announcement provides contact details for investor relations and media enquiries but does not disclose specific financial metrics or performance data in the RNS notice itself.
retail_take: Routine disclosure of interim results filing; substantive market impact depends on actual H1 2026 financial performance details contained in the full report, which is not summarised in this announcement.

headline: SCPLC Half Year Results 2026 -  Part 2
brief: Standard Chartered H1 2026 interim results Part 2: detailed risk and capital review with credit impairment analysis.
summary: Standard Chartered's H1 2026 risk review shows credit exposure increased $72.8bn to $939.4bn, driven by higher derivative instruments (+$16.4bn), FVOCI assets (+$27.9bn), and customer loans (+$12.5bn). Credit impairment charges totalled $446m (H1 2025: $336m), with $234m attributable to Middle East conflict overlays and elevated downside scenario weightings (60% vs 41% prior year). Stage 1 performing loans remained strong at 94% of portfolio; stage 3 coverage ratios improved in WRB and CIB.
retail_take: Non-event for retail investors. Technical regulatory filing with risk metrics and governance detail; credit quality remains solid but geopolitical headwinds and heightened uncertainty driving conservative provisioning.

headline: Mass production PO for Pro-AV display solution
brief: Nexteq's Densitron brand wins mass production order for Pro-AV display solution with Tactila® technology from new customer.
summary: Densitron has secured a mass production purchase order for an integrated Pro-AV display solution featuring Tactila® haptic technology from a new professional audio-visual customer. The order commences in H2 2026 with unit volumes increasing incrementally over four years. This win validates Nexteq's strategic shift from hardware-only displays to higher-value integrated system solutions and demonstrates Tactila® commercial traction across broadcast and professional applications.
retail_take: Market likely reads positively as material contract win validating Tactila® investment and strategic pivot to systems; incremental four-year ramp suggests meaningful revenue runway, though unnamed customer and early-stage timing limit immediate impact quantification.

headline: New Contract Win with APCOA Parking
brief: Crimson Tide wins three-year contract with APCOA Parking to deploy mpro5 platform across UK operations.
summary: Crimson Tide plc has secured a new three-year contract with APCOA Parking (UK) Limited, part of Europe's leading parking management group operating 1.8 million spaces across 13 countries. mpro5 will be deployed across car park auditing, hospital site patrols, and civil enforcement officer patrols. The win follows competitive selection against two rival platforms and expands an existing relationship already live in Ireland, demonstrating customer confidence and the platform's configurability across multiple operational workflows.
retail_take: Positive signal: demonstrates mpro5 market traction, validates product-market fit with large multi-site operators, and shows ability to expand within existing customers—supporting management's growth strategy and adding contracted recurring revenue.

headline: Billington Leadership Appointments
brief: Billington Holdings announces two senior leadership appointments effective 1 August 2026.
summary: Kevin Campbell moves from Managing Director of Billington Structures to Group Strategic and Special Projects Director, after 4.5 years driving operational improvements and growth. Dan Duffield, currently Sales Director at Billington Structures, succeeds Campbell as Managing Director, bringing nine years with the company and extensive operational and commercial experience since 2007. CEO Mark Smith praised both appointments as well-deserved, highlighting their strategic fit for supporting long-term Group development and transformation initiatives.
retail_take: Internal promotion of proven talent signals management confidence and continuity; no material risk indicated. Likely read as routine positive governance by the market.

headline: Rio Tinto 2026 Half Year Results Presentation
brief: Rio Tinto releases 2026 half-year results with presentation and webcast hosted by CEO Simon Trott and CFO Peter Cunningham.
summary: Rio Tinto PLC released its 2026 half-year results on 29 July 2026 at 8:30am AEST (11:30pm BST on 28 July). The results presentation, slides, and webcast recording are available on the company's investor relations website. CEO Simon Trott and CFO Peter Cunningham hosted the webcast followed by a Q&A conference call, providing shareholders with financial performance updates and strategic insights.
retail_take: Routine regulatory announcement of results release; substantive market impact depends on actual financial performance disclosed in the presentation and slides, not yet detailed in this notice.

headline: Appointment of Non-Executive Director
brief: Breedon appoints Louis Eperjesi as non-executive director, effective early 2027, bringing extensive building materials sector experience.
summary: Louis Eperjesi, former CEO of Tyman plc and with senior roles at Kingspan, Baxi, Lafarge and Caradon, joins Breedon's board in early 2027. He will sit on Audit and Risk, Remuneration, Nomination, and Sustainability Committees. Eperjesi currently serves as non-executive at Howden Joinery, Ibstock, Trifast and Accsys Technologies, stepping down from Ibstock prior to joining Breedon. Chairman Amit Bhatia cited his international materials market experience and change management expertise.
retail_take: Appointment of an experienced non-executive with strong sector credentials and established board presence adds strategic depth; routine but positive governance signal for a FTSE 250 company.

headline: Q2'26 Earnings Release and Conference Call
brief: Vaalco Energy schedules Q2 2026 earnings release for August 6, with conference call on August 7.
summary: Vaalco Energy (NYSE: EGY; LSE: EGY) will release second quarter 2026 earnings on Thursday, August 6, 2026 after NYSE close, followed by a conference call Friday, August 7 at 8:00 a.m. CT. The Houston-based independent energy company operates production, development and exploration assets across Gabon, Egypt, Côte d'Ivoire, and Equatorial Guinea. Call details: US toll-free (833) 685-0907; UK +44 20 3769 4533; webcast available at www.vaalco.com.
retail_take: Routine earnings announcement scheduling; no material information disclosed. Market impact depends on Q2 results when released August 6, not on this notice itself.

headline: Execution of Amendment rig contract to drill MOU-6
brief: Predator Oil & Gas amends rig contract to drill MOU-6 well in Morocco from August to October 2026, followed by Trinidad Snowcap-3 operations.
summary: Predator Oil & Gas has executed an amendment to its drilling contract with Intrepid Drilling Limited for Rig 101, extending operations from 1 August to 1 October 2026 at the MOU-6 well site in Morocco. The company plans a three-month drilling and testing programme across two continents, with MOU-6 as the first well followed by Snowcap-3 in Trinidad. CEO Paul Griffiths highlighted confidence in well planning based on 2021-2023 drilling data, with potential de-risking of gas and oil resources for near-term production pending regulatory approvals.
retail_take: Operational execution catalyst signals Predator advancing exploration programmes after 15-month rebuild period; market likely positive on activity de-risking but should note regulatory approval requirement before production.

headline: Notice of Results and Investor Presentation
brief: Ondo InsurTech to report FY2026 results on 30 July; investor presentation scheduled for 31 July via Investor Meet Company.
summary: Ondo InsurTech PLC will publish full year results for the period ended 31 March 2026 on 30 July 2026. Executive Chairman Gregory Mark Wood CBE, CEO Craig Foster, and CFO Kevin Withington will present findings via Investor Meet Company on 31 July 2026 at 14:00 BST. The live presentation is open to existing and potential shareholders, with pre-event questions accepted until 30 July 09:00 BST.
retail_take: Routine regulatory announcement providing results timing and presentation logistics; no material updates disclosed; market reaction will depend on results substance rather than this notice.

headline: Maiden Independent 43-101 Resource at Akoko
brief: Hamak Strategy announces maiden 210,430oz gold resource at Akoko project in Ghana; commission PEA for potential low-capex mine.
summary: Hamak Strategy (LSE: HAMA) reported its first independent NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate for the Akoko Oxide Gold Project in southwest Ghana: 210,430oz at 0.76g/t Au (3.9m tonnes Measured & Indicated at 0.83g/t; 5.2m tonnes Inferred at 0.71g/t). Over 124,000oz represents shallow oxide material within 50m of surface at 0.81g/t Au with metallurgical recoveries of 85-94%. The company has optioned 100% acquisition at US$15/oz (US$9/oz cash plus share consideration). Hamak will proceed to independent PEA targeting 20,000+ oz annual production via simple open-pit heap-leach operation. Resource remains open at depth and along strike; only 35% of 15km geochemical anomaly drilled.
retail_take: Market likely reads positively: maiden resource validates exploration thesis, attractive acquisition terms at US$15/oz imply good value entry, and near-term production potential via shallow oxide mining. However, this is exploration-stage with significant execution risk ahead; high-risk venture combined with company's Bitcoin treasury exposure.

headline: Appointment of Joint Corporate Broker
brief: Accesso Technology appoints Shore Capital as joint corporate broker alongside Deutsche Numis.
summary: Accesso Technology Group PLC (AIM: ACSO) has appointed Shore Capital Stockbrokers Limited as joint corporate broker, working alongside Deutsche Numis, which continues as nominated adviser and existing corporate broker. The leisure and entertainment technology solutions provider serves over 1,100 clients across 31 countries. The appointment expands the company's corporate advisory and broking resources.
retail_take: Routine capital markets housekeeping; appointment of additional broker support is standard practice and typically signals preparation for corporate activity or liquidity expansion, though not material in itself.

headline: Notification under UK Listing Rule 6.4.9R(2)
brief: Plus500 director Tami Gottlieb appointed to external board role at Canadian real estate company.
summary: Tami Gottlieb, an Independent Non-Executive Director at Plus500, has been appointed as an External Director of Almadev Real Estate Inc., a Canadian company listed on the Tel-Aviv Stock Exchange, effective 27 July 2026. The appointment is disclosed under UK Listing Rule 6.4.9R(2) requirements for director related-party positions.
retail_take: Routine regulatory disclosure of a director's external appointment; immaterial to Plus500's operations and financial position; likely market neutral as no conflicts apparent.

headline: Quarterly Activities and Cash Flow Report Q2 2026
brief: Thor Energy reports strong Q2 2026 results with natural hydrogen readings up to 3% and secures major 464km seismic survey contract.
summary: Thor Energy ended Q2 2026 with A$2.815m cash, down A$499k from Q1, after spending A$66k on exploration. The HY-Range Project Phase-2 geochemistry survey recorded natural hydrogen concentrations of up to 3% (30,000ppm), approximately 60,000 times background levels, validating three priority exploration areas. Thor awarded Velseis a 464 line-kilometre 2D seismic survey contract (Q3-Q4 2026), fully funded from existing reserves following non-core asset divestments. Additionally, Thor expects to receive the first of three annual deferred payments of A$1.3125m on 1 September 2026 from the FRAM JV sale to Tivan Limited.
retail_take: Positive signal: encouraging hydrogen geochemistry results and funded seismic programme de-risk the exploration thesis, with near-term cash inflow reducing funding concerns and extending runway to approximately 5.6 quarters of operations.

headline: Funding
brief: Premier African Minerals raises £550k via share issuance to fund Zulu lithium project operations.
summary: Premier African Minerals completed a subscription raising approximately £550,000 before expenses through issuing 4 billion new ordinary shares at 0.01375 pence per share. Proceeds will support operational continuity at the Zulu Lithium and Tantalum Project in Zimbabwe, including mining and stockpiling activities, while the company negotiates an extension of the Long Stop Date with Canmax Technologies. Total issued share capital post-issuance will be 50.1 billion shares. Admission to AIM expected around 3 August 2026.
retail_take: Heavy dilution (4bn new shares) to fund operational burn suggests weak balance sheet and project funding challenges. Market likely views this negatively absent concrete Canmax deal progress or production milestones.

The trust operates an unconstrained, long-only emerging markets strategy focusing on small and mid-cap companies, maintaining a concentrated portfolio of 25-30 holdings. The manager employs active ownership with bespoke ESG+C engagement strategies to drive value creation across portfolio companies.
retail_take: Routine monthly disclosure providing investors with regular fund performance and portfolio data; no material news or strategic changes signalled in announcement itself.

retail_take: Routine disclosure for employee share scheme exercise; modest dilution immaterial to capital structure; no operational or strategic implications signalled.

headline: Proposed Board Changes
brief: RentGuarantor appoints three independent Non-Executive Directors and promotes two existing leaders to strengthen governance.
summary: RentGuarantor proposes appointing Ben Thompson (40+ years financial services experience, former ULS Technology CEO), Maya Klein Wassink (corporate finance and capital markets adviser with 25+ years property development experience), and Simon Jackson (35+ year chartered accountant, former CEO of WH Ireland and Brooks Macdonald) as independent Non-Executive Directors. Amanda Bower, current Business Compliance Manager, is proposed as Executive Director/Chief People and Risk Officer, and David Cliff transitions from Non-Executive to Executive Director of Research and Innovation. Appointments subject to regulatory due diligence, completion expected this quarter.
retail_take: Significant board strengthening with highly experienced financial services and governance specialists, signalling management confidence in executing growth strategy post-AIM listing. Market likely to view positively given calibre of appointees and focus on AI development.

retail_take: Routine disclosure of employee share scheme awards; typical for companies with established option plans. No material impact signalled.

headline: Non-Executive Director and Corporate Appointments
brief: Oriole Resources appoints experienced mining NED Dr Mike Armitage, new Company Secretary Rod Venables, and broker Zeus Capital.
summary: Dr Mike Armitage, with 40 years' mining industry experience including 30 years at SRK Consulting, joins as Non-Executive Director from 1 August 2026 to support development of Cameroon projects (Mbe: 1.66Moz gold resource; Bibemi: 460koz resource). Rod Venables appointed Company Secretary for corporate governance support. Zeus Capital appointed broker, replacing previous adviser, bringing natural resources sector expertise and planned research coverage.
retail_take: Board strengthening with credible technical expertise ahead of Cameroon project development phase signals management confidence in transition from exploration to production; broker appointment suggests increased investor relations focus.

summary: Oliver Plunkett, Non-Executive Director and CEO of Ocean Infinity (SRT's 14.63% shareholder), purchased 190,456 ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 at 77.9575 pence each via LSE. Following the transaction, Plunkett holds 785,456 shares directly (0.29% of issued capital) and maintains indirect beneficial interest via Ocean Infinity in 39,943,422 shares (14.63%). The purchase signals continued confidence from a connected party in maritime surveillance and fisheries monitoring technology provider.
retail_take: Director purchase at current market price suggests confidence in company fundamentals; however, as routine PDMR disclosure with no material change in Ocean Infinity's controlling stake, likely treated as non-event by markets.

headline: Director purchase of CLNs
brief: Sunda Energy CEO Dr Andy Butler acquires £400k convertible loan notes from Alumni Capital; no conversion plans.
summary: Dr Andy Butler, CEO of AIM-quoted oil & gas firm Sunda Energy, has agreed to purchase £400,000 principal value of unsecured convertible loan notes (CLNs) from Alumni Capital Limited for £432,000. The CLNs were originally issued as part of financing for the conditional acquisition of Matahio Energy NZ Limited announced 8 April 2026. Dr Butler has indicated he does not currently intend to convert the notes. Terms remain unchanged and the underlying transaction targets completion in September 2026, pending New Zealand government approval.
retail_take: CEO investing personal capital in company debt signals confidence in the acquisition completion and underlying asset value; suggests insider belief in near-term catalysts. Market likely views positively as vote of confidence.

Molaoi Drilling Update
brief: Molaoi drilling extends high-grade zinc-germanium mineralisation deeper than expected, with grades strengthening at depth.
summary: Hole HMO-019 at Rockfire's 100%-owned Molaoi zinc deposit in Greece returned six mineralised intersections including 0.10m @ 27.8% Zn and 84.1g/t Ge (one of the highest recent germanium values), plus 3.30m @ 18.9% Zn at 261m depth. Results extend mineralisation 50m deeper than previous hole HMO-018, with stronger grades suggesting potential grade increase at depth. Drilling continues upgrading the Inferred Resource to Indicated status; results from HMO-020 awaited. New drilling rig expected September/October; feasibility study advancing with comminution and ore-sorting tests planned.
retail_take: Positive momentum on exploration upside at a critical minerals asset; deeper, higher-grade intersections support near-term resource upgrade path and long-term feasibility study progression, likely supporting sentiment.

retail_take: Routine share buyback execution at consistent pricing; signals capital deployment but provides limited insight into strategic direction or market outlook.

headline: June 2026 Quarterly Activities Report
brief: Greatland Resources beat FY26 guidance with 328,987oz gold production; FY27 output expected to decline as investment ramps.
summary: Greatland produced 328,987oz gold at A$2,179/oz AISC in FY26, exceeding 260-310koz guidance. June quarter yielded 79,100oz at A$2,312/oz with 86.8% recovery rates. Cash position strengthened to A$1,289m (debt-free) with A$302m operating cash flow. FY27 guidance: 260-300koz at A$2,900-3,330/oz AISC. Company commencing Havieron pre-production capex (A$365-435m) and Telfer growth investment (A$315-335m), with first Havieron gold expected FY29.
retail_take: Strong operational beat and balance sheet support long-term growth story, but FY27 production decline and elevated AISC guidance signal near-term headwinds from heavy capex and lower ore grades.

headline: 1st Quarter Results
brief: Maruwa reports Q1 FY2027 results with 11.7% sales growth to ¥19.3bn and 5.8% operating profit rise to ¥6.3bn.
summary: Maruwa Co achieved Q1 FY2027 net sales of ¥19,267m (+11.7% YoY), operating profit ¥6,348m (+5.8%), and net profit ¥4,466m (+15.2%). The Ceramic Components segment grew 10.1% to ¥16,785m; Lighting Equipment surged 23.7% to ¥2,482m on LED demand. Company revised full-year FY2027 forecasts upward to ¥93.3bn sales (+25.3%) and ¥33.7bn operating profit (+34.9%), citing strong telecom and semiconductor demand. Total assets reached ¥165.5bn with equity ratio of 91.5%.
retail_take: Positive earnings beat with significant full-year guidance raise reflects genuine demand acceleration in telecom/semiconductor; capex expansion plans suggest management confidence, though geopolitical headwinds and FX assumptions (158 yen/USD) present execution risks.

headline: Half Yearly Report to 30 June 2026
brief: Imaging Biometrics swings to H1 2026 profitability on 6% revenue growth and 32% cost cuts; IB Clinic gaining clinical traction.
summary: Imaging Biometrics returned to profit in H1 2026 with £73,852 net income versus £89,652 loss prior year. Revenue grew 6% to £416,270; gross profit £414,536. Administrative expenses fell 32% to £325,860, driving operating profit of £88,678. IB Clinic neuro-oncology platform advancing clinical adoption; EAF151 Phase II data presented at ASCO showed superior automated imaging biomarker performance. GaM paediatric cancer programme positioned for partnership; FDA designations in place but development early-stage with 30 September 2029 PRV deadline.
retail_take: Profitable inflection on cost discipline and clinical validation likely reads positively; however, profitability modest and GaM upside heavily caveated and contingent on unproven partnership and regulatory approval by tight deadline.

headline: 75% ARR Growth Drives Revenue & Profit Visibility
Half Year Trading Update and Notice of Results
Musensi Hill Rare Earth Elements Project, Tanzania
brief: Amigo Resources completes initial geological mapping at Musensi Hill REE project in Tanzania, confirming carbonatite system model.
summary: Amigo's geological team completed systematic mapping and sampling at the Musensi Hill rare earth elements project in Tanzania. Initial XRF screening identified encouraging geochemical indicators including potassium oxide (9-11.7%), calcium oxide (up to 15.1%), strontium (up to 7,000 ppm), and phosphorus pentoxide (up to 7.29%). Results support a multi-phase alkaline-carbonatite interpretation. The company emphasises the screening did not include full REE analysis and cannot determine grade or economic potential. Next phases include complete REE analysis, mineralogy, petrography, and definition of drill targets.
retail_take: Early-stage exploration results are geologically encouraging but commercially non-committal; no mineral resource defined and much work remains before determining economic viability, likely a modest positive for sentiment.

headline: Half Year Trading Update
brief: Kooth reports H1 2026 revenues of £30.8m with Adjusted EBITDA of £5.0-5.4m, up sharply from £1.6m prior year.
summary: Digital mental health provider Kooth delivered H1 2026 revenues of £30.8m (H1 2025: £32.1m), with planned California product tapering and £0.7m FX headwind offset by Michigan contract gains. Adjusted EBITDA expected £5.0-5.4m versus £1.6m prior year, reflecting strong California user engagement and return to profitability. Net cash position strengthened to £23.1m (H1 2025: £15.3m). California's Soluna platform achieved 187k registrations and external validation via DHCS impact report and Governor's Children and Youth Behavioral Health Initiative.
retail_take: Strong EBITDA recovery and cash generation offset modest revenue decline; California traction and government validation suggest sustainable growth trajectory, likely positive market reception despite revenue headwinds.

headline: Half-year Report
brief: IPF posts H1 pre-exceptional PBT of £47.4m, customer numbers up 5%, receivables up 17%; acquisition by Bidco completing 4 August.
summary: International Personal Finance reported H1-26 pre-exceptional profit before tax of £47.4m (down 5% YoY from £49.9m), reflecting continued investment in growth. Customer numbers increased 5.4% to 1.743m, customer lending grew 18.5%, and closing net receivables rose 17.4% to £1,169.9m. Impairment rate widened to 10.0% from 8.3%, driven by stronger lending growth in new channels. The company maintains £107m headroom on facilities and 48% equity-to-receivables ratio. Recommended acquisition by IPF Parent Holdings (Bidco) expected to complete 4 August 2026 subject to Court sanction on 31 July; special dividend of 15p per share declared, conditional on completion.
retail_take: Solid operational performance with controlled credit quality offset by expected profitability headwinds from IFRS 9 impairments and strategic investment. Acquisition completion imminent reduces forward guidance relevance for independent shareholders; market focus shifts to deal closure and dividend certainty.

headline: 1st Quarter Results
brief: PayPoint reports Q1 FY27 revenue down 6.4% to £39.5m but says it's on track for market expectations with reorganisation embedding successfully.
summary: PayPoint's Q1 FY27 net revenue fell 6.4% to £39.5m from £42.2m, driven by Network Services (down 6.5% to £21.6m) and Love2shop (down 9.8% to £7.0m), offset partly by Digital Payments & Open Banking growth of 4.1% to £3.2m. CEO Nick Wiles highlighted successful business reorganisation embedding with improved retailer engagement, positive momentum in new business wins (Scottish Power, housing clients), and Love2shop's July campaign delivering 103% growth in cards sold. Management expects greater performance weighting to H2 and remains confident in meeting FY27 market expectations; a Capital Markets Day is scheduled for 29 September 2026.
retail_take: Mixed signals: revenue decline against tough comparatives and challenging consumer backdrop offsets by operational improvements and new business traction; market likely cautious until H2 execution demonstrates recovery trajectory.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: PSH repurchased 32,646 shares at average price of $50.36 on 28 July 2026.
summary: Pershing Square Holdings repurchased 32,646 public shares on 28 July 2026 through agent Jefferies at an average price of $50.36 USD. The buyback comprised 22,370 shares on LSE (PSH ticker) at 3,787 pence average and 10,276 shares (PSHD ticker) at $50.28 average. NAV per share was $76.01 USD as of 21 July. Post-buyback, PSH has 173.55 million shares outstanding with 37.41 million held in treasury.
retail_take: Routine share buyback execution at modest scale; buyback pricing below NAV ($50.36 vs $76.01) suggests potential shareholder value accretion, though announcement provides no strategic context or forward guidance.

headline: Half-year Financial Report
brief: LMS Capital NAV falls to 33.0p per share from 35.9p as managed realisation strategy continues with £1.6m capital return.
summary: LMS Capital's NAV declined £2.4m to £26.6m (33.0p per share) at 30 June 2026 from £29.0m (35.9p) at year-end 2025. The decrease reflects a £1.6m capital return in February, £0.2m portfolio losses, offset by £0.2m FX gains from sterling weakness. Cash fell to £2.6m from £6.8m due to capital returns, Dacian loan funding, and Castle View debt repayment. Key holdings: Dacian (energy, £10.8m), Castle View retirement living (£9.4m), and Opus venture fund (£3.0m). Board expects clarity on main asset liquidity by end-2026/early 2027.
retail_take: Modest NAV decline reflects continued capital returns and portfolio challenges; limited near-term catalysts visible, though Board expects strategic clarity within six months, unlikely to move shares meaningfully absent material realisation progress.
